key_insight: In isolated focal dystonia—not cancer—AI-derived brain imaging features helped prioritize rare variants in RAP1GAP, TNN and ITSN2.
clinical_relevance: The findings may advance dystonia gene discovery but do not establish a diagnostic test or treatment.
method: Trained DystoniaGeneNet, a 3D convolutional neural network, on T1-weighted MRIs from 40 familial laryngeal dystonia patients and 40 healthy controls.
Used model predictions to guide variant prioritization and family segregation analyses in 214 exomes.
Evaluated genetic findings in 738 independent exomes and two additional case-control datasets.
evidence_signal: The model correctly classified 85.7% of 21 independent familial cases; genetic analyses identified rare RAP1GAP and TNN variants segregating with disease and highlighted ITSN2 variants in predicted familial-like sporadic cases.
watch_item: Small imaging training and familial evaluation cohorts limit generalizability, and the supplied abstract truncates the functional results.
paper_title: Perisynaptic matrix gene variants underlie DystoniaGeneNet endophenotypes in isolated focal dystonia
